steps.title: Autocorrelation, ARCH effects and normality of monthly log changes

result.white_noise: autocorrelation remains (smallest Ljung-Box p = 0.0391 across lags 1-24)

arch_effects.conclusion: No ARCH effects detected: a GARCH model is not warranted at this frequency; constant variance is adequate.

normality.conclusion: Not normal (skewness 1.65, kurtosis 8.87 vs 3): Gaussian intervals will misstate tail risk; consider a Student-t distribution.

result.note: With many lags, ~5% of ACF/PACF values exceed the band by chance alone; isolated small spikes are weak evidence.

steps.title: Same diagnostics on DAILY log changes

result.white_noise: autocorrelation remains (smallest Ljung-Box p = 7.72e-11 across lags 1-24)

arch_effects.conclusion: ARCH effects present (volatility clustering): a GARCH-type variance model is warranted.

normality.conclusion: Not normal (skewness 0.86, kurtosis 10.13 vs 3): Gaussian intervals will misstate tail risk; consider a Student-t distribution.

setup.loss_scale: log scale (errors are approximately relative errors)

shock_concentration.note: Share of the benchmark's total squared one-step error coming from its largest 5% of errors. High values mean a few shocks dominate the loss, which makes accuracy differences hard to establish.

reading_guide: rel_rmse < 1 means lower error than the benchmark; dm_p < 0.05 means the difference is statistically significant.
Nominal coverage is 0.80 / 0.95: higher means intervals are too wide, lower means too narrow.
log_score: higher is better; it rewards calibrated intervals and fat tails where they are needed.
calm / turbulent split origins by trailing 12-period volatility (above vs below the median).
